results.name: shared_digit_far_targets
results.description: For targets more than 15 beyond the examples' range, yes-rate when the target shares a last digit with some example minus when it shares none; observed > null means people use surface digit similarity more than the model's rules capture.
results.code:
# name: shared_digit_far_targets
# description: For targets more than 15 beyond the examples' range, yes-rate when the target shares a last digit with some example minus when it shares none; observed > null means people use surface digit similarity more than the model's rules capture.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    d = np.maximum(np.nanmin(ex, axis=1) - t, t - np.nanmax(ex, axis=1))
    share = np.any(np.mod(ex, 10) == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    far = d > 15
    m1 = far & share; m0 = far & ~share
    a = r[m1].mean() if m1.any() else 0.0; b = r[m0].mean() if m0.any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)

results.name: below_minus_above_range_near
results.description: Yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the set minimum minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the set maximum; observed > null means people extend downward more (or upward less) than the model's symmetric interval prior predicts.
results.code:
# name: below_minus_above_range_near
# description: Yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the set minimum minus yes-rate for targets 1-10 above the set maximum; observed > null means people extend downward more (or upward less) than the model's symmetric interval prior predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    b = (t < lo) & (lo - t <= 10); a = (t > hi) & (t - hi <= 10)
    rb = r[b].mean() if b.any() else 0.0; ra = r[a].mean() if a.any() else 0.0
    return float(rb - ra)

results.name: primacy_near_first_minus_last
results.description: In multi-example sets, yes-rate for targets within 5 of the first-shown example (and not within 5 of any other) minus that for targets within 5 of the last-shown example only; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means example order matters, which the order-blind model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: primacy_near_first_minus_last
# description: In multi-example sets, yes-rate for targets within 5 of the first-shown example (and not within 5 of any other) minus that for targets within 5 of the last-shown example only; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means example order matters, which the order-blind model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = s.str.count(",").to_numpy() + 1
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    dist = np.abs(ex - t[:, None]); dist[np.isnan(dist)] = 1e9
    idx = np.arange(len(t)); last = dist[idx, np.clip(n - 1, 0, ex.shape[1] - 1)]
    first = dist[:, 0]; close = (dist <= 5).sum(axis=1)
    mf = (n >= 2) & (first <= 5) & (first > 0) & (close == 1)
    ml = (n >= 2) & (last <= 5) & (last > 0) & (close == 1)
    a = r[mf].mean() if mf.any() else 0.0; b = r[ml].mean() if ml.any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)

results.name: span_scaled_extension
results.description: Yes-rate for targets within 10 outside the range of wide-span sets (span >= 30) minus that for narrow-span sets (span <= 10, multi-example); observed > null means people's out-of-range extension scales with span more than the model's fixed-scale Erlang prior allows.
results.code:
# name: span_scaled_extension
# description: Yes-rate for targets within 10 outside the range of wide-span sets (span >= 30) minus that for narrow-span sets (span <= 10, multi-example); observed > null means people's out-of-range extension scales with span more than the model's fixed-scale Erlang prior allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = s.str.count(",").to_numpy() + 1
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1); sp = hi - lo
    d = np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi)
    near = (d >= 1) & (d <= 10) & (n >= 2)
    mw = near & (sp >= 30); mn = near & (sp <= 10)
    a = r[mw].mean() if mw.any() else 0.0; b = r[mn].mean() if mn.any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)

results.name: round_target_effect
results.description: Among sets not all multiples of 10, yes-rate for targets that are multiples of 10 minus other targets, both lying outside the examples' range; observed > null means people over-accept round numbers beyond what the model's rule mixture predicts.
results.code:
# name: round_target_effect
# description: Among sets not all multiples of 10, yes-rate for targets that are multiples of 10 minus other targets, both lying outside the examples' range; observed > null means people over-accept round numbers beyond what the model's rule mixture predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    allten = np.all(np.isnan(ex) | (np.mod(ex, 10) == 0), axis=1)
    out = (t < np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)) | (t > np.nanmax(ex, axis=1))
    rt = np.mod(t, 10) == 0
    m1 = ~allten & out & rt; m0 = ~allten & out & ~rt
    a = r[m1].mean() if m1.any() else 0.0; b = r[m0].mean() if m0.any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)

results.name: late_minus_early_yes_rate
results.description: Overall yes-rate on trials in the upper half of trial_index minus the lower half; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means responding drifts over the session, which the stationary model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: late_minus_early_yes_rate
# description: Overall yes-rate on trials in the upper half of trial_index minus the lower half; nonzero observed vs a ~0 null means responding drifts over the session, which the stationary model cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    med = np.median(ti); a = ti > med; b = ti <= med
    x = r[a].mean() if a.any() else 0.0; y = r[b].mean() if b.any() else 0.0
    return float(x - y)

results.name: gradient_near_minus_mid
results.description: Yes-rate for targets 1-5 beyond the examples' range minus yes-rate for targets 11-25 beyond it; observed > null means human generalisation falls off more steeply just outside the range than the model's Erlang interval prior produces.
results.code:
# name: gradient_near_minus_mid
# description: Yes-rate for targets 1-5 beyond the examples' range minus yes-rate for targets 11-25 beyond it; observed > null means human generalisation falls off more steeply just outside the range than the model's Erlang interval prior produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    d = np.maximum(np.nanmin(ex, axis=1) - t, t - np.nanmax(ex, axis=1))
    near = (d >= 1) & (d <= 5); mid = (d >= 11) & (d <= 25)
    a = r[near].mean() if near.any() else 0.0; b = r[mid].mean() if mid.any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)

results.name: four_minus_two_examples_outside
results.description: Yes-rate for targets outside the examples' range in 4-example sets minus that in 2-example sets; observed more negative than null means people tighten generalisation with more examples faster than the model's size principle predicts.
results.code:
# name: four_minus_two_examples_outside
# description: Yes-rate for targets outside the examples' range in 4-example sets minus that in 2-example sets; observed more negative than null means people tighten generalisation with more examples faster than the model's size principle predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    ex = s.str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = s.str.count(",").to_numpy() + 1
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy(); r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    out = (t < np.nanmin(ex, axis=1)) | (t > np.nanmax(ex, axis=1))
    m4 = out & (n == 4); m2 = out & (n == 2)
    a = r[m4].mean() if m4.any() else 0.0; b = r[m2].mean() if m2.any() else 0.0
